utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. General, may I remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence which still applies. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, General. General, do you remember that yesterday we completed the testimony when I showed you an Official Note by an investigating judge Ognen Stavrev who was not able to enter the village of Ljuboten neither on the 12th nor on the 14th of August, to perform the on-site investigation. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that the on-site inspection attempts were made by both the judge and the prosecutor it was obvious that they had information about any reasonable grounds to suspect that there were dead people in the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if you agree with me, General, it would be the Prosecutor only who could start a procedure before -- against some persons if the identity of those persons were known and that procedure would be taken before investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Otherwise, the police has no powers to interrogate people as witnesses. They could only gather some information and compose an Official Note on that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct, upon a request of the prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the police could hold a citizen, a suspect or any other citizen, in their premises for up to 24 hours. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that, persons can be held only if that decision is made by the investigating judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But in other premises, not inside the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The police otherwise had no access to the judicial procedure they can place before a judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I am pointed some mistake in the transcript. Maybe it is a different interpretation but it is not a mistake so we may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When a person is detained for the duration of detention when they need to in a hospital is that correct that then it is detention guards who are securing his presence at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, court police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The court police is outside of the competences of the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are in the Ministry of Justice.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, the guards in the detention and in the remand prison Sutka are not under the Ministry of Interior. They under the Ministry of Justice. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for this information. So after it was not possible to make this on-site investigation, you stated twice already that your committee tried to gather information down your lines of command, down the SVR Skopje lines and down other lines in the hierarchy, to gather information about the events taking place in Ljuboten and you stated that most of the work was done by Goran Mitevski as the president of the committee. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. All the material that's arrived would go directly to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can we agree that these are materials that otherwise arrive from police stations up the line of command to the analytics department or to you, your cabinet or through the criminal police, they would come to the cabinet of the under-secretary for the forensic techniques and the information that would arrive on the basis of the operational action, Ramno. Would this be the information that you could have had available when compiling your report?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were available but I will repeat again they were all at the directors, Goran Mitevski's.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you stated, you relied also on the information that you gathered from your subordinates, from the sector Skopje as well as the part of the ministry of the criminal police which relied on the information that arrived via these routes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, also, that answering the Prosecutor's question you stated that you were convinced that also some persons were interrogated in relation to the events that took place?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the police stations there were several peoples who were interviewed, but I could not tell you the number or the police stations where the interviews were taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And these interviews would be generally a task for the criminal police?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. And this is why I don't have any more precise information because this is it outside of the scope of my work. It does not belong to the uniform police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, if, General, witness M83 would testify before this court that after the event he was called to provide additional information about the actions that he had taken, that would be in -- that would correspond to this knowledge of yours, that the interviews in the field were conducted before you had compiled this information?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It might be appropriate to clarify whether witness M-083 was testifying in regard to providing additional information to the committee that this witness was a member of, or was he asked to provide additional information two years later to a second committee, established by a second minister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't have the page of transcript here, but it is certain that this witness testified that Blagoja Toskovski called him sometime after the event and asked him to provide additional information. If it is needed, I will find the page in the transcript where this witness testified about that. But my question is simple and I could refrain from asking this witness that question because I could not directly quote the words of the witness but they are in the transcript, and the witness has answered my question in that way if my learned colleague remembers that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Would it not be simple just to confirm whether he is speaking of his committee or the second committee?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this witness could not know about the other committee because he was not in the Ministry of Interior then and this it is clear from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you said that some people were giving statements and that they were interviewed, did you mean that they were interviewed during the work of your first committee?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the inspectors from OVR Cair mostly interviewed several persons. That was while the decision related to the first committee was still valid.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So these interviews that you are discussing were made before you compiled your report on the 4th of September, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say with 100 per cent certainty, but as far as I remember it was so. I remember this from the discussions with the director Mitevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And would it be correct -- actually, would you agree with the fact that in page 1439 the witness interviewed before this Court testified that he had been called by the authorised officers to provide additional information about what he knows in relation to the events where he personally participated. It was -- those were the interviews conducted at that time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it still seems unclear to the Prosecution whether witness M-083 was -- what time-period witness M-083 was referring to, whether he was referring to the time-period of August/September 2001 or perhaps the time-period of the second investigative committee that was not established until 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The uncertainty is not with the evidence of this witness but with the evidence of M-083.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you very much. I will leave this question. The testimony of that witness is very clear in the page of transcript that I indicated. It is not necessary for me to ask this witness to repeat what another witness has already testified about before this Court. Thank you very much and I apologise for this interruption.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that during the work of your committee you received requests from the crisis management body, coordination committee to submit certain information to them about the events that took place in Ljuboten, and your information about those events?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think there was such a request. It is not a committee, it is a coordination body for crisis management. It was chaired by the minister Filipovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And apart from the fact that you stated that you received some information down the line of command from Bliznakovski is it also correct that the criminal police for the sector Skopje was also headed by an experienced professional, Petre Stojanovski, and neither you nor director Mitevski had any reason to doubt the information received from him?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course we had full confidence in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When we discussed the responsibilities of the minister established by the Law on the Bodies of Civil Service, is it correct that one of his responsibilities was to inform the government about the situation in the area covered by him?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This goes without saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the minister has the duty to act upon the conclusions of the government. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware, General, that the report you compiled was reviewed in a government session as well?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I think it had been reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the document in tab 12 -- actually, in tab 114, I apologise. This is 65 ter 1D489, 1D4424, and the English is 1D4425. This is a conclusion from a government's meeting, which states: "Information on events and developments in the area of Skopje, village, Ljuboten. The government reviewed the information about the events and developments in the area of the Skopje village, Ljuboten, and adopted it as a material to -- as information material together with suggestions and comments proposed by the coordinated body for crisis management and those that emerged during the session. Furthermore, the government concluded that the minister of the interior and the Ministry of Defence should prepare a joint information with the most recent data in connection with the events and developments in the area of the Skopje village of Ljuboten, which they should submit for government's review." Is it correct, General, that from this conclusion of the government it can be seen that this is a coordinated body and that the government reviewed the information compiled by you?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course it is correct, looking at this document, and I think that this comes from the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would seek to tender this document as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 1D134, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document there tab 108. This is 65 ter 1D488. 1D4416 is the Macedonian, while 1D4420 is the English text. You see here that the minister Ljube Boskoski submits a note to the coordinated body for crisis management and precisely to the minister Ilija Filipovski whom you have mentioned containing an information about the events in Ljuboten, and of course -- and also information about the events in Tetovo. Does this also corroborate the notion that the minister informed all government bodies and the government itself very openly about the findings you made reviewing the Ljuboten event?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would seek to tender this document as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the document in tab 109 --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I propose that I didn't wait for your decision. I would seek to tender this document as Defence exhibit, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 1D135, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in paragraph 109 -- in tab 109, 65 ter 241. N000-9253 is the Macedonian, and N000-9251 is the English. If we look again at this information, you will agree with me that this is an information that is sent as a memo to the coordinated body, not only about the Ljuboten events, but also it contains a brief review about the Tetovo events. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would kindly ask the counsel to move closer to the microphone or use another microphone. We can't hear her clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 1D136, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before we move on and discuss other measures to be undertaken after your report was compiled, I would like to ask you to look now at this information in tab 113, and it is now P378. Otherwise, we have it in e-court as 65 ter 239 as a Prosecutor's Exhibit. And I would like to ask you to immediately look at the last page. So this is an opinion, and it starts on the page 5 of this information, and it ends on page 6, while the English text starts on page 4 and ends at page 5. I would like to look at the last paragraph of this opinion of yours, and I would like to ask the interpreters to interpret from the Macedonian text, because I think there are certain problems with the English translation. And in this opinion of yours you state the following: "In conditions of an objectively justified absence of written documents from the on-site investigation and post-mortem of the bodies found in the village of Ljuboten, Skopje region, and in order for the analysis of the issue at stake to be comprehensive and multi-facetted, it is necessary that the competent structures in the Republic of Macedonia undertake legal actions exhumation of the bodies in presence of experts as well as representatives of the interested international organisations, which will have as its consequence undertaking of all necessary legal actions aiming towards ascertaining all relevant facts and reaching the answer to this open essential issue for this case." Do you see this conclusion that you've made?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that the absence of on-site inspection, as it is noted here, and a post-mortem was an objective fact due to which you could you not say anything more in this information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. I am repeating this several times already, without an on-site investigation, nothing more could have been undertaken that what had already been.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that as you state here the following actions could be undertaken only by certain competent structures in the Republic of Macedonia and this competent structures for such affairs are only the investigating judge and the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is due to the fact that it is the exclusive competence of the court to order exhumation and post-mortem; such request or such measure could not be ordered by the police to anyone. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. We proposed this, but we could not order this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that without exhumation and post-mortem of the bodies, first you could not know how many people were killed, what was the status of those people, what killed those people, and under which circumstances they were killed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it also correct that writing this information, you immediately wanted for the procedure to be completely public and transparent so you proposed that there would be international entities participating in the process of exhumation and post-mortem?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So compiling this information you never hid anything that could not be ascertained but you offered a direction of how one could arrive to additional evidence about what took place in the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering this proposal that you made, and after the information was reviewed by the government, if I understood your answer well, the one you gave to the Prosecutor, you were not involved any longer in the work of the committee because it was by compiling this information that the -- that the committee finished its part of work. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But is it also correct that as a member of the collegium and also because you yourself needed to provide additional information regarding certain measures, you were still aware of measures that were undertaken in the ministry for these events to be clarified in a legitimate way?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. And I still wonder why it was necessary to stop the activities. And it is -- there is never in the applicable legislation in Macedonia that a deadline within which an investigation needs to be completed, stipulated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that the minister himself was not very satisfied with the fact that until the end of the work of the committee you could not gather all the relevant information and then he presented this dissatisfaction of his very often in the collegium?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not answer briefly by just saying yes or no but I remember very well General Mitevski told me several times that the minister was making pressure on him at least for us to work more intensively. I told him that I took all the measures that I could have taken within the realm of my competencies regarding the uniformed police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct if I reminded you of the fact that the assistant to the minister for the city of Skopje, Zoran Efremov, who had a traffic accident that year and he had difficulties in performing his duty was also by the pressure from the minister for this situation to be investigated to the greatest possible extent and that he finally accepted to leave this duty because he thought that he couldn't do more than what had been done before?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with this conclusion because I met him -- I met Mr. Efremov often walking on crutches from the minister's office and he was not very happy.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it also correct that at that time, at the beginning of September, the minister had suspended also Ljupco Andonovski, head for state security of Skopje, because he believed that more could have been done in order to learn yet additional information about what actually took place, and that only after additional clarification, Ljupco Andonovski was reassigned to his duty. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honestly I don't remember details. I know there were personal shifts but when exactly and were they related to this, I could not confirm.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that you yourself proposed exhumation and post-mortem, and it could have been only proposed formally by the prosecutor and enforced then by investigating judge, is it then true that the Ministry of Interior could not wait any longer for the prosecutor and the judge to do it on their own motion, so already on the 7th of September such motion was sent to the investigating judge and to the public prosecutor for --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sorry for the interruption, but it appears that my colleague is asking the witness to put himself in the mind of the then minister of interior, Mr. Boskoski. Because she is asking the witness, Isn't it true that the -- I heard minister. Did I read it wrong? I now see Ministry of Interior. But it simply appears to me that she's asking this witness to place himself in the mind of the minister and I don't think this witness can do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says ministry in this line. I never said minister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I suggest that it's a question too far, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are aware, General, that the ministry raised an initiative with the public prosecutor's office and with the court for the exhumation and the post-mortem to be performed?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think yes. I think there were several occasions on which this was proposed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please look at the document in tab 120, that is 1D33 exhibit N000-7332, Macedonian page, and N000-7332-ET, the English page. In the upper left corner you can see that it comes from the Ministry of the Interior, the office of the public security and the date is 7th of September, 2001. It is directed to the prosecutor's office and to the duty investigating judge of the Basic Court II in Skopje. We see in the middle of the document there is a motion for exhumation and autopsy while at page 4 of this document, that is N00335, we can see that it is signed by the director Goran Mitevski. Is this a document of the ministry, General, that raises an initiative to the competent bodies to carry out the exhumation and the autopsy?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if we look at the last page of this document, N000-7334,--

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction 7335.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the English version is 7334-ET we can see the reason why this initiative was raised whereby it is written that in addition, we think that the proposal for exhumation and autopsy is grounded it should be accepted in order to determine the identity of the five bodies and to establish the cause of the death of the five persons from the Ljuboten village. That is exactly what you proposed in your information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the exhibit found in tab 121, that is the Exhibit P55. N002-1 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the upper left corner you can see basic public prosecutor's office, arrow number 1098/01 dated 10th of September, 2001, signed by the deputy public prosecutor Dragoljub Cakic. This is ET N002-1148-1. From this document you can see that the public prosecutor immediately reacted at the initiative it was sent from the Ministry of the Interior and asked to conduct certain investigating measures. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And according to the law on criminal procedure when the perpetrator is unknown, only certain investigating measure could be undertaken. Investigation could not be requested. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to the Law on the Criminal Procedure of the Republic of Macedonia an investigation could only be carried out against known perpetrators and for a specific act. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If the perpetrator is unknown, then the prosecutor could only ask to carry out certain investigating measures that is the case in this event?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the public prosecutor has the right to ask for additional gathering of information in relation to certain events.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 you see that the public prosecutor's office in relation to this case is acting pursuant to the regulation in the law upon the written initiative of the Ministry of Interior. So is it correct that this proposal that the prosecutor is authorised by law to raise and to initiate according to the initiative that was sent to him by the Ministry of Interior. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. But I would add that there were a lot of oral initiatives in order to start these activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, I would like to ask you to look at the document found in tab 123. That is exhibit 1D46, 1D1947, Macedonian version and 1D14-- 1948 in the Macedonian [as interpreted] version. In the upper right corner, it-- can you see the number --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. This must be exhibit 1D46, yes, we have it displayed now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the upper right corner we can see the number 1D--

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have the English translation displayed? We still don't have it. 1D1948.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Macedonian text in the upper right corner we see the number ID.number.601/01. This number is not recorded in the English translation. This is the number of the file under which certain cases registered in the court. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see that this is an Official Note of the investigating judge Dragan Nikolovski, and if we look at its contents we can see that on the 14th of September, 2001, the judge organised a meeting at the institute for forensic medicine and criminalistics whereby the representatives of this institute were present as well as the public prosecutor Dragoljub Cakic as well as representatives of the minister of the interior, from the homicide department, from the sector of the Ministry of Interior of Skopje. Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the judge also very soon after he received the proposal from the public prosecutor, reacted and started to carry out measures that are necessary in order to initiate an exhumation procedure for the bodies?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he reacted immediately -- that the court reacted immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look now at the document in tab 124. That is exhibit 1D73. The page is N005-0754, and the English version is N005-0754-ET. This is an Official Note composed by two employees of the Ministry of Interior, and if we look at the very beginning of this Official Note it speaks that on the 14th of September in the premises of the institute for forensics medicine and criminology a consultative meeting has been held at which the judge, investigating judge Dragan Nikolovski was present and it was related to the exhumation and the autopsy of the persons in Ljuboten. This is an Official Note that also confirms that the investigating judge held a meeting in relation to prepare the exhumation and the autopsy. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think this the same meeting at which -- for which the investigating judge has provided a note. We can see that these are the two colleagues from the Ministry of Interior who have filed this Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if we look at the last paragraph on the first page, we will be able to see that it reads: "Dr. Aleksej Duma, affirmed his willingness to effect the exhumation and autopsy following the previously received order from the IJ," meaning investigating judge, "and also stated that in order to avoid any subsequent manipulation of the autopsy results of the buried remains in the village of Ljuboten, he will arrange for supervisors to be present during the investigation in the form of competent individuals from the Skopje office of The Hague Tribunal. Do you agree with me that not only you but also there were other participants who wanted to find out what has happened in Ljuboten asked hat the international community and this Tribunal are present when this exhumation and autopsy were to take place?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at document in tab 127. That is exhibit P99. The page is 1D1895, and the English version is 1D1900. General, as we can see, this is an information coming from the public prosecutor's office of the Republic of Macedonia dated the 18th of November, 2001. So is it correct if we look at this title that this information also refers to the questions of taking certain measures in order to clarify the situation about what has happened in Ljuboten in the period of 10th, 11th, 12th, 13th and 14th of August, 2001. So the state public prosecutor's office was attempting to carry out this exhumation and autopsy. Would you agree with me that this is line with what you know, that the public prosecutor Stavre Dzikov participated in some meetings in the ministry. That is the person signing this information.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, completely correct. The very title of the information speaks of the content although I could not comment the content because I have not seen it until now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask to you look at the last page of this information which is 1D1899 and the English version is 1D1902. In the last paragraph of this information, the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia writes that it is of utmost importance to point out that the locals of the village of Ljuboten never asked to meet the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia, nor have they submitted any written reports of information on the events happening on the indicated date in the sense of Article 144, paragraph, of the Law on Criminal Procedure which would provide us using -- which would allow us to use the institute for -- for -- about the rumours heard. So if we can see here, none of the local residents asked any-- for any activities in the -- and they have never -- is this information in line with your knowledge that the Albanian population at that time was not -- did not want to contact the state bodies at all at that time?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this confirms it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As we saw from your information, and that was the information from the meeting held together at the institute of forensic medicine, you would agree with me that your efforts to involve the international community were ongoing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But is it correct that you felt that the international community does not want to give you the appropriate assistance, assistance that was given in the case of Aracinovo although you did not know what were the real reasons for this to happen. Was this your opinion at that time as I say it now?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't surely say that did want to help the representatives of the international community, especially the NATO people who I contacts with most frequently, but their advice by them was they would cause a greater incident if they would attempt to do it. Although I personally think that if they tried to explain the Ljuboten residents in some correct manner that a judicial investigating procedure is in course, that an on-site investigation is going to be carried and the police is not going to cause any problems, I'm sure that that would be completed in the best manner. But I will repeat again. Unfortunately, that did not take place.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document found in tab 132. I would like to ask you to look at the document found in tab 129 first. That is Exhibit P55. The number is N002-1146-10188 [as interpreted]. The English is N002-1234. General, in the -- again in the upper left corner we can see that the public prosecutor's office of the Republic of Macedonia on the 21st of January, 2002 -- as Exhibit P55, number N002-1146-088, and the English version is N002-1234. So the state public prosecutor, Stavre Dzikov, with this information, asks for a meeting on 31st of January, 2001 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 30th of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- in respect to the events in Ljuboten on the 10th, 11th, and 12th of August, 2001. Do you see that this is a call for a meeting?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this communication also speaks that the competent bodies, the public prosecutor and the court, are taking measures in order to carry out an exhumation and an autopsy but it is obvious that they were not able to do that by themselves?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This should be a meeting that took place on the 30th of January, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please now look --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 30th of January, 2002. The information is of 22nd of January, 2002, and that is a call for a meeting that needs to take place on the 30th of January -- the text makes it wrong, actually. This is supposed to be 2002, not 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please look into tab [No interpretation]. [In English] meeting for Ljuboten case. On 30 January -- Do you hear the translation, general?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I hear it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: "[In English] On 30 January 2002 EUMM attend a meeting at the public prosecution department regarding events in Ljuboten on 10 to 12 August 2001. Among those present were deputy public prosecutor Dragoljub Cakic, Professor Aleksander Duma of the department of forensic medicine and president of appellation court Ms. Filimena Manevska, Mr. Andrzej Szydlik of the ICTY, Ambassador Klaus Voellers of NATO, EUMM and OSCE represented the IC. Public prosecutor Mr. Stavre Dzikov chaired the meeting. The local authorities explained very briefly that the security forces had acted against terrorists in Ljuboten during three days from 10 to 12 August 2001 after a mine incident in area on 10 August 2001 in which eight soldiers were killed and another eight wounded. They stated that there is unconfirmed information about 12 to 13 people having been killed in Ljuboten during the action by the security forces and about five of those having been buried in the village. "Comment, the Human Rights Watch report of the incident claims that the operation left ten civilians dead and resulted in the arrest of more than 100 men, and refers to a government newscast on 12 August 2001 to the effect that minister of interior, Mr. Ljube Boskoski was present at the scene that day. As it turned out the meeting of 30 January 2002 concerned the identification of the five bodies allegedly buried in Ljuboten since the events of August 2001. Ambassador Voellers raised the issue of investigating what actually happened, if crimes were committed and if so, by whom, would be held responsible. Mr. Dzikov avoided giving a straight answer to the question, claiming that investigation -- investigating teams were ready to enter the village on 12 and 14 August but had been prevented from doing so. The focus of the discussion remained on the possibility of conducting an exhumation in Ljuboten to ascertain the identity of the five bodies. "The ICTY presented a number of conditions regarding a possible exhumation in Ljuboten. There should be no uniformed police present in the exhumation site and no special forces. Security should be provided by NATO in the presence of OSCE and EUMM. Max two bodies should be removed from the site at one time to be taken to Skopje for examination and then returned to the site before any more bodies were taken to Skopje. "The Macedonian presence at the scene should be limited to what would be essential for the investigation. The ICTY should be provided with copy of all relevant documentation and if relatives of those buried want to be present at the exhumation site, this should be permitted and ICTY requested a written commitment from the authorities to act in compliance with these demands at the request of Mr. Dzikov," and so on. [Interpretation] General, I would like to ask you two things in respect to this report of NATO about a meeting of 30th of January. Is it correct that the state prosecutor clearly mentions here that the competent bodies of the Republic of Macedonia were not able to enter Ljuboten on the 12th and the 14th?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct that the prosecutor confirms it but also that the ICTY representative confirms it in the last paragraph of this letter, thereby suggesting to avoid having uniformed police over there. This is sometime the beginning of 2002, and the event took place in mid-2001 so even five or six months later the situation is such that the police is not able to make an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was my next question. Is it clear here, General, that international community is of the position that the police should not make an on-site investigation in the village?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague showed you the Human Rights Watch report published on the 5th or 6th of September, 2001, and you said that you have heard something about the content of that report in the media. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the recommendations that the Human Rights Watch directs to the government of the Republic of Macedonia, it is requested to carry out an impartial investigation by impartial bodies and already then, so that was the beginning of September, it has been said that the police should not -- the Ministry of Interior should not participate in that investigation. Is that fact contained in the report helping you to understand the problems why you, as a police, were not able to carry out certain actions?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't even today say what are the reasons. I can only assume but without facts I would not be able to make a conclusion. Although, it was really strange.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct, General, that the residents of the village of Ljuboten didn't want to communicate with police representatives at that time?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was such a problem for a long period of time. I very well recall the implementation plan to return the police in this crisis areas. The Ljuboten village, in that time, was one of the peaceful areas, but after these events it entered the group of crisis villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you look, General, now at the document in tab 131. This is exhibit 1D9, page 1D1140. This document, General, contains the notes compiled at the meeting between the members of the deceased family -- the families of the deceased people in Ljuboten and representatives of international organisations such as the OSCE and the ICTY. Do you see this document before you?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only in English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see here in paragraph 2 that this meeting was held on Friday, March the 8th, 2002. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the second page, 1D1141, at the very bottom it says: "[In English] There was initial resistance by the spokesman of the crisis community Mr. Saliu Kenan about the involvement of the Republic of Macedonia agency. Feeling obviously running high and there was talk of noncooperation by the villagers." [Interpretation] What was said by the head of the crisis centre at the meeting? Does it also show that the villagers were not ready to discuss with the representatives of state authorities of Macedonia and do you agree with that from what you know from 2001?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask to you look at the document in tab 132. This is Exhibit P55, number N002-1146-048, and the English version is ET-N002-1194. You are certainly aware, General, that under the conditions established by the ICTY at this meeting of January the 30th, eventually started the preparations for the exhumation and autopsy of the corpses in Ljuboten. Are you aware of the fact that this exhumation and autopsy were being prepared?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that at that time I was at the police academy, but followed this events through the media, the television, and press. And I know that they did occur.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the exhibit you have before you, this is an order from the investigating judge of the Basic Court Skopje II, you can see on the left corner see this number, ED number 601-01. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the upper right corner there is an ID number 601/01, this is the number that you saw before when the exhumation was proposed. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an identification number, ID number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you see the preamble of this order from the judge, you will see that even when the international community involved and helped for the exhumation and autopsy to start, that this issue is still recorded under the number, under the same number as it was recorded when it was proposed and the preamble itself says that the investigating judge of Basic Court Skopje II, Dragan Nikolovski, acting upon the proposal and undertaking certain investigation measures recorded under arrow number 1098/01 dated 10th of September, 2001, submitted by the basic public prosecution office Skopje on exhumation and autopsy in accordance with Article 244 and 246 of the code of criminal procedure adopted on 3rd April 2002. So if we see this, you will agree that the initiative of September the 7th that the prosecutor accepted on September the 10th and the investigating judge immediately acted upon could not be executed unless the international community accepted to participate in these exhumation and autopsy procedure. Is this entirely clear from this document?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is entirely clear. This is the moment after which the procedure started to get normal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But the procedure to know the facts, the true facts was in fact started by the Ministry of Interior, by proposing an exhumation an autopsy?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we go back now to the commission that was proposed by the minister would you agree with me that by selecting Goran Mitevski as an honest and experienced connoisseur of the police affairs that in fact the minister appointed the true person that would know how and in which way and pursuant to the laws the issues related to Ljuboten would be adequately cleared out. Is this conclusion correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But all your -- all the efforts that you invested could not give adequate results because, from the very beginning you didn't have the support from the international community and neither did the citizens of the -- the residents of the village of Ljuboten wanted to cooperate and give support to the authorities of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague showed to you also a document related to the European commission on torture and inhuman treatment. I think this is how it is called, torture prevention and inhuman treatment. Do you remember that kind of document?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this document, as you could see, when it was shown to you, that this information or that this report was submitted on January 16th, 2003. Do you remember that this was a date after which you were not anymore with the ministry and after Ljube Boskoski was not minister anymore?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was over a year. That was not at the interior ministry anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But this was -- document was marked for identification but we will now go back to that document as of now. It is it important to say that the visit that is referred to a meeting held on 21st to 26th of October 2001. Were you told at the time that your investigation was --

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone from the international community ever say to you that the investigation that you had conducted was a sham investigation? Has anyone told you that ever?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one ever told me something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Has ever the government of the Republic of Macedonia told you that what you did was something that was invented and faked and not true effort to -- to reveal the truth?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the government adopted that information.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could please the counsel slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that acting upon the conclusion of the government to make a joint information with the defence ministry you submitted a draft information to the Ministry of Defence and proposed the way in which the work should continue? Please look at the document in tab 115.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note would Ms. Residovic be so kind to slow down a little. It is really difficult to interpreter precisely at this pace.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 65 ter 1D -- Your Honour, I have been rightfully warned by the interpreters to slow down, but yesterday I said I would finish before the break, but I think I would need 15 minutes more after the break and this is the reason why I am speeding up in order to comply with my promise given to the Court. So would you allow me to -- 15 minutes to continue after the break to continue my cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The other way of complying with your time indications is not to ask about so many things or to ask about them at such length. I have mentioned that to start to encourage a greater attention to the need for each question. But you will certainly be able to finish after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. General, before you you have a letter that minister of the internal affairs sent to the Ministry of Defence. It is signed by the sate secretary of the ministry of internal affairs, Branko Bojcevski. Do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I do, addressed to the state secretary of the defence ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The subject of this letter to the Ministry of Defence is a proposal for a joint report, preparation for joint report. Do you remember that before we saw the conclusion of the government that it is necessary to compile a joint information, do you remember this conclusion adopted by the government?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this letter from the Ministry of Internal Affairs offering to the defence ministry a working draft of a document and offering a way in which to proceed is in fact a rapid reaction to fulfilling the conclusions of the government. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to these concrete measures that you try to undertake and you undertook in order to understand exactly what happened in the given dates in and around Ljuboten, could you please tell me, General, that the ministry, at the same time, was very seriously looking into the suggestions related to some problems within the ministry itself, and as of 2001 started with systemic changes in the ministry in order to eliminate an impossible mistakes in the work of the police officers?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The changes were being done all the time, but at the end of 2001, after the framework agreement, as far as the equitable representation of the non-majority part of the population, a very serious part of this changes started in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that 109 Albanian police officers had been employed in September. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That year, also a training of several hundreds of police officers started in accordance with NATO standards. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. In the beginning of 2002, if it is relevant for the Court, I would clarify that as of September 2001, the training of 109 police officers was conducted by the American embassy in Skopje, while in 2002 the training was taken over by OSCE.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And your decision to transfer to an institution that would do the training of new personnel in order to have police officers that would be released of all [indiscernible] and past burdens is one of the reasons why you requested, in fact, to be transferred to the police academy. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was a new challenge for me and I was very pleased to start that job.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the same time, all the police stations were sent and all police administrations were sent instructions with precise -- precisely requiring respect of human rights and all the rights of people that are brought in, in police stations. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the interior ministry we also prepared some small flyers containing instructions for all the police officers on the ground, both active police officers and reservist police officers and there were also large posters containing the instructions of how a person that was brought in a police station should be treated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just one question before the break. At the time the cooperation with Danish competent institutions with the Helsinki committee of OSCE started, and together with them, a small brochure was prepared on the same issues and it was delivered to all police stations. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Minister Boskoski signed also the agreement with the bar association of the Republic of Macedonia because he thought that the obligatory presence of a lawyer at the police station would be the best way to prevent any possible abuse of power. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is correct. I wanted to say this before. Minister Boskoski is also signature of the -- of the agreement for the training of ethnic police officers, if I can call them like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe it is now time to adjourn, and I won't have -- I won't need more than 15 minutes after the break, and I will try to be even shorter. Thank you for allowing me to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, very briefly. The Chamber will recall that during the first session there was some discussion about the testimony of witness M-083 and the Prosecution made an objection because it was unclear to the Prosecution whether witness M-083 had spoken with Mr. Blagoja Toskovski during the work of the first committee, August of 2001 or during the work of the second committee in early or late 2003 and the Prosecution has now had an opportunity to see the transcript of witness M-083's testimony and it's clear from the record that witness M-083 was referring to August 2001, that is, the time-period of the committee for which this witness was a member, and so the line of questioning of my colleague was -- was proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Ms. Residovic's recollection was accurate then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank my learned colleague. Before I start asking questions, I would like ask Your Honours to receive the tab 115 as Defence exhibit. This is a proposal to prepare a joint report with the Ministry of Defence which has been shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 14 -- 1D490.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 137, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, when my learned colleague the Prosecutor asked you you stated that you did not have good relations and you don't have good relations to this very day with the third member of the committee. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you as a member of the collegium of the minister surely know that during that time there were problems in the work of your colleague, the under-secretary for criminal police, that he was often absent from work because of medical checkups?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the Ohrid agreement was signed, you personally and your associates were tasked with returning the people from the place -- to the places from which they were expelled. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People who were displaced from their homes and also was tasked with establishing a normal regime of police patrols in those regions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You remember that already that in early Autumn had you a conference together with the minister and Goran Mitevski a press conference where you explained which were the tasks for the police that would enable the return of people to their homes?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that this conference took place in the round hall in the government's building.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will remind you, actually, I will put to you, General, that the Prosecutor has offered P286 -- P276 as a video recording of that press conference and it was received and the text of that video recording is in tab 148, and this exhibit states that in that conference you stated that the plan jointly prepared for this return in several stages and that the first stage involves places under the least risk and in Skopje this would, among the others, Ljuboten. But my question is, General, is it correct that later because of the significant problems with the return of the police to Ljuboten there was a change of plan, and Ljuboten has been characterised as a location under great risk. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could be please look at the document in tab 149. That is 65 ter 1D484, 1D4332 is Macedonian, and 1D4333 is the English text. You have in front of you a document from the police department, 23rd of 11, 2001 is the date, and you have signed it, if I remember correctly?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I prepared this plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is the annex to the main -- to the general plan, and from the second paragraph one can see that there was change with regard to the return of the security forces in the following settlement and in line 1 it says in sector Skopje, Gornje Mojance, Orlanci [phoen] and Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to --

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 1D138. And as the transcript did not record the previous one, it was 65 ter 1D490 received as exhibit 1D137, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look now at the document in tab 150, General. This is 65 ter 403, N004-9830, and the English is N004-9830-ET. And I would like to ask to you move to the third page immediately, that is N004-9832. And the English, N004-9831-ET, and it continues on the next page. You can see in this information about the security situation in the crisis regions that the area of Skopje is described. In the second paragraph it is stated, second paragraph of the Macedonian text: "In the Skopje region on the 3rd of December, 2001, in the area of village Ljuboten at the location Basinec and Kales Mara a group of several armed persons attacked the positions of the army of the Republic of Macedonia." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were this incident and the similar ones which took place in Ljuboten and around it, the reason why the security forces could not enter Ljuboten before 2002?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look now at the document in tab 151. This is 65 ter 1D461, 1D4246. This is a document which is part of 65 ter 268, and this is why I will give his English enumeration as well. This is a plan for return of the security forces into the regions where the displaced persons were returned. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is correct, although I have the version in the English language here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But it says plan for the return of the security forces [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... Return of the displaced population.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know it, because we gave an English copy of it to the representatives of the international community.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this plan of -- for return also forces with regards to the Skopje region, the village of Ljuboten as a place which could not be entered in the first stage. It is, rather, a settlement which is still under security risk and it should be entered into in a later stage. Do you remember that this plan provided this?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we would seek to tender this document as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As well as the previous document, 65 ter 1D484, which -- no. 65 ter 403, that is the information about the security situation. And it is in tab 150.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 403 will be received as exhibit 1D139, and 65 ter 1D461 as exhibit 1D140, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you refer that when asked by the Prosecutor you actually explained your conversation with Mr. Boskoski at the moment when the topic of the discussion was the mode in which to provide for the Albanian population and you then stated that the -- your place of birth does not contain mixed population while Ljube Boskoski was born where Albanians and Macedonians lived together. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And knowing Mr. Boskoski, you can confirm before this Court that he held no prejudice on either ethnic, national or religious basis towards the peoples or towards his associates?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are completely right. I would also add that we had visited his native village, Celopak, several times and apart from his neighbours, Macedonians, he also shook hands with the other residents, Albanians. They were true neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So he grew up together with the Albanians and he has friends Albanians to this very date. Is it so?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is correct. I have never heard him say a bad word about the Albanians in general.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: His deputy throughout the crisis was an Albanian, and he are friends to this very date?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the last question I wish to ask you, General, you know that pursuant to the framework agreement the Law on Amnesty was in preparation and it was adopted?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And am I understanding it correctly if I state that this amnesty was provided for any person who was related to the conflict, without making any distinction or division on national or ethnic or religious basis?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It applied to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that this law provided that if there would be a reasonable ground to suspect that a person had committed a crime but the procedure was not instigated still, the procedure would not be instigated at all?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that pursuant to this law, if a procedure against a person had been instigated, then the procedure needed to be terminated. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that if a person had been sentenced, then the serving of the sentence needed to be terminated immediately?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that pursuant to that law, only later, so after the adoption of the law in February 2002, even if it was found that a police officer had abused the powers of his office, then the bodies of the Republic of Macedonia would not be able to instigate a criminal procedure against him, because that would be in breach to the Law on Amnesty. The only exception was the possibility for the procedure to continue if it had already been instigated before the International Tribunal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have concluded my cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We understand from what you said yesterday, Mr. Apostolski, that you have no questions. Is that still the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I have no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Galevski, my colleague just asked you a couple of questions about the amnesty law that was adopted in February 2002, and you explained that if it -- even if it had been found that a police officer had abused his powers, the bodies of the Republic of Macedonia would not be able to instigate a criminal procedure against him because that would be in breach of the law of amnesty. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, would -- would it have been possible for the Ministry of Interior to discipline a police officer for an abuse or abuses committed prior to the adoption of the Law on Amnesty in February 2002?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there is no retractive application.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't know what that means. Can you say that in layman's terms?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law applied only to cases related to the conflict, which means that if a police officer had abused powers in another way, of course the disciplinary measures would apply.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If a police officer had abused his powers -- if a police officer had abused his or her powers in some way -- in a way that was related to the conflict, could the Ministry of Interior still initiate disciplinary proceedings or enforce disciplinary proceedings against that officer, even after the passage of the amnesty law?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the Law on Amnesty is clear and the disciplinary responsibility is much lesser and insignificant compared to the criminal responsibility. So if the public prosecutor and investigating judge are not investigating a procedure for a person to be tried ex officio, then the disciplinary responsibility becomes minor, insignificant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Does the Law on Amnesty that was adopted in February 2002 bar, prohibit, Ministry of Interior from disciplining its police officers?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the question is very complex. Certainly the Ministry of Interior has forever and during the tenure of Mr. Boskoski had the orientation to instruct and train its officers and make them upgrade their skills, in order for them to --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to perform the tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What I asked you can be answered in just yes or no or I don't know. I will repeat my question again. Does the Law on Amnesty that was adopted in February 2002, did that law prohibit the Ministry of Interior from disciplining police officers for abuses committed during the conflict? Can you say yes, no, or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't answer this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, I don't know how to answer this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. You told my learned colleague this morning that at the end of 2001 systematic changes began to be made in the Ministry of Interior in order to eliminate mistakes in the work of police officers. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters kindly ask for the noise in the courtroom to be minimised. People are shuffling of pages. It really impedes us in our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were these reforms that were implemented beginning in late 2001, were these encouraged by representatives of the international community then working in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because the intentions for such reforms dated a lot earlier than 2001, a lot before the conflict. Thanks to the representatives of the international community, they were actually implemented in the practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What kind of mistakes were these reforms intended to eliminate?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what mistakes you refer to. The mistakes that employees are held responsible of are enumerated in the collective agreement, while the reforms in the police started after the -- in accordance with the -- with the obligations coming out from the stabilisation association agreement with the European Union which was signed somewhere in April 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you there. Page 33 of the transcript this morning, my colleague put to you the proposition that in late 2001 systematic changes began to be made in the Ministry of the Interior to eliminate mistakes in the work of police officers, and you agreed with that. So tell us, please, what kind of mistakes were these reforms intended to eliminate, or if you don't know, you can say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to respond in details, but, generally, yes, because the police had inherited from the previous regime and it was high time to change it in accordance with European standards. Therefore to make an organisation and the police that would be in accordance with police in the European countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. On Tuesday, General, at page 3660 of the transcript, you explained that Minister Boskoski was one of the rare ministers of the interior who convened the collegium of his closest advisors and subordinates. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my personal opinion, different from other ministers, he almost regularly held such staff meetings. His -- the minister before him did not that so regularly and his successors almost never had such staff meetings. He nurtured this team-work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
